entries.name: Devilforged
entries.flavor: The Devilforged are weapon masters who harness the mysterious powers of Devil Fruits through infused items, wielding incredible abilities that bend the forces of nature and magic to their will. By synthesizing the lineage factors of these fruits into their gear, Devilforged enhance their weapons with explosive elemental power, shaping their combat style through relentless experimentation. Their bound equipment becomes an extension of their very being, capable of great destruction, but always tied to the unique essence of the Sea Devil’s curse.

subclassIntro.text: Devilforged have a variety of methods of infusing Devil Fruit powers into their equipment and items. However, whichever type of items you tend to infuse the most will determine your Devilsmith style.

features.name: Devil Fruit Infusion (Spellcasting)
features.text: You have mastered the art of infusing items with Devil Fruit powers through the use of “Green Blood”, which you have acquired by some means. Green Blood is made up of the synthesized lineage factors of Devil Fruits, which allows you to replicate the magical powers of Devil Fruits through your equipment. Through the use of these artificially infused items, which serve as your spellcasting focus, you can use a variety of powers (spells) to aid you in battle or adventure. Devil powers are the equivalent of “Spells” in 5th edition, and devil power slots are the same as “Spell Slots”. Make sure to view the “Casting a Spell” section in the Player’s Handbook for understanding Spellcasting in 5th Edition D&D. Devilforged powers count as Devilforged Spells in Chapter 4.

sections.name: Natural Abilities (Cantrips)
sections.text: At 1st level, you know two cantrips of your choice from the devilforged spell list in Chapter 4, and can use them as natural abilities. You learn additional devilforged cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Natural Abilities (Cantrips) Known column of the Devilforged table.

sections.name: Devil Power (Spell) Slots
sections.text:
The Devilforged table shows how many Devil Power (Spell) slots you have to cast your devil powers of 1st through 5th level. The table also shows what the level of those slots is; all of your slots are the same level. To cast one of your Devil Powers of 1st level or higher, you must expend a Power (spell) slot. You regain all expended power (spell) slots when you finish a short or long rest.
For example, when you are 5th level, you have two 3rd-level power (spell) slots. To cast the 1st-level power (spell) witch bolt, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a 3rd-level spell.

sections.name: Devil Powers (Spells) Known of 1st Level and Higher
sections.text:
At 1st level, you know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the devilforged spell list.
The Spells Known column of the Devilforged table shows when you learn more devilforged spells of your choice of 1st level or higher. A spell you choose must be of a level no higher than what’s shown in the table’s Slot Level column for your level. When you reach 6th level, for example, you learn a new devilforged spell, which can be 1st, 2nd, or 3rd level.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the devilforged spells you know and replace it with another spell from the devilforged spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

sections.name: Devil Power (Spellcasting) Ability
sections.text:
Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your devilforged spells, so you use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a devilforged spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier

sections.name: Infused Item (Spellcasting Focus)
sections.text:
You produce your devilforged powers (spells) and effects through a special devil fruit-infused item you possess. You must have a power (spellcasting) focus - specifically some kind of weapon, armor, tool, or other item that is infused with devil fruit powers - in hand when you cast any power (spell) with this (spellcasting) feature. You must be proficient with the item to use it this way.
Once you have chosen one item or piece of equipment you wish to have infused, it becomes your power (spellcasting) focus. You cannot have more than one item infused with devil fruit powers in this way. If you wish to move the essence stored within your current infused item of choice into a new item or create a new infused item after losing your old one, you must spend 1 hour during a long rest to move the Green Blood from your old weapon into the new item and removing them from the old item. You must be proficient with this new item. In addition, you may choose to infuse items that are connected to your body, but not made of flesh. For example, a cyborg’s iron fists may have devil fruit powers infused into them through green blood, without the cyborg itself having consumed a devil fruit, because they are technically not a part of the cyborg’s natural body.
Due to the infusion of multiple devil fruits’ essence into your item through the use of Green Blood, the exact devil fruit power it possesses may not be clear. Instead, your item has an infusion of many different powers you have collected through researching, hunting, and foraging for devil fruits. It should not be treated as a creature that has consumed a devil fruit power, but instead as a tool that grows in power with it’s user over time. In addition, the item has the weaknesses of a devil fruit user in that it cannot be used as a power (spellcasting) focus while it is more than half-submerged in water or touching seastone.

features.name: Devilsmith
features.text: At 1st level, you have developed a particular style of devilsmithing which determines the types of equipment or items you specialize at infusing with. You can choose between Blade Smithing, Devil Bombardier, Firearm Smithing, Gear Smithing, Mechadevil, or No Mi Trainer, all detailed at the end of the class description. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Sea Devil’s Emanations
features.text:
In your exploration of the origins of Devil Fruit powers through synthesizing their lineage factors, you have uncovered the true nature of the Sea Devil’s energies that imbue these powers, now capable of being released from your infused item.
At 2nd level, you gain two sea devil emanations of your choice. When you gain certain devilforged levels, you gain additional emanations of your choice, as shown in the Emanations Known column of the Devilfoged table. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the emanations you know and replace it with another emanation that you could learn at that level.

features.name: Infuse Devil Fruit
features.text:
At 3rd level, you learn to infuse Devil Fruit powers into non-magical weapons, merging the fruit’s abilities with the item. You can infuse one weapon at a time. Infusing a new weapon dispels the previous infusion. The infusion lasts indefinitely but can be removed prematurely with a full week of focused effort.
Infusing a fruit into an item requires 8 hours of uninterrupted work and access to both the fruit and the item. The infused item retains its original properties and gains additional abilities based on the type of fruit.
If the item is broken or the infusion is removed, the devil fruit is cast back out onto the open seas and can be found using the “Finding a Devil Fruit” rules in Chapter 7 of the Dungeons and Devil Fruits Player’s Handbook.
At 8th level, you may infuse any number of non-magical weapons.

sections.name: Body Enhancer Paramecia Infusion
sections.text:
Body Enhancer fruits grant physical augmentation powers that extend to the infused weapon.
Damage Boost. Increase the weapon’s damage die by one size up to d12 (e.g., d6 to d8, d8 to d10).
Enhanced Strikes. Add a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls equal to the fruit’s rarity modifier starting with uncommon. This effect does not allow the weapon to bypass resistances or immunities.
Fruit Effect. With your DM’s help, the weapon gains one feature from the fruit’s stat sheet. The feature cannot be the fruit’s awakening or any that would grant the user a resistance or immunity.

sections.name: Environment Altering Paramecia Infusion
sections.text:
Environment Altering fruits affect the surroundings, enabling infused weapons to manipulate the battlefield.
Fruit Effect. With your DM’s help, the weapon gains one feature from the fruit’s stat sheet. The feature cannot be the fruit’s awakening or any that would grant the user a resistance or immunity.
Fruit Spells. Using your weapon as the source of the spells, you may cast a spell from the devil fruits spell list using the Devil Fruit Infusion Charges table.

sections.name: Substance Generator Paramecia Infusion
sections.text:
Substance Generator fruits create materials, which the infused weapon uses for offense or utility.
Substance Generation. With your DM’s help, the weapon gains one of it’s non-awakening substance generation features from the fruit’s stat sheet. The substance comes out of the weapon.
Fruit Spells. Using your weapon as the source of the spells, you may cast a spell from the devil fruits spell list using the Devil Fruit Infusion Charges table.

sections.name: Special Paramecia Infusion
sections.text:
Special Paramecia fruits grant unusual and versatile abilities to the infused weapon.
Elemental Damage. The weapon deals an additional 1d6 elemental damage (closest to the fruits element as you can) on a hit and the weapons attacks ignores resistances to non-magical damage.
Fruit Effect. With your DM’s help, the weapon gains one feature from the fruit’s stat sheet. The feature cannot be the fruit’s awakening or any that would grant the user a resistance or immunity.
Fruit Spells. Using your weapon as the source of the spells, you may cast a spell from the devil fruits spell list using the Devil Fruit Infusion Charges table.

sections.name: Zoan Infusion
sections.text:
Zoan fruits channel animalistic traits into the infused weapon.
Enhanced Strikes. Add a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls equal to the fruit’s rarity modifier starting with uncommon. This effect does not allow the weapon to bypass resistances or immunities.
Beastial Morph. The weapon’s range can increase by up to 5 ft. as the zoan beast sprouts from the handle. When you attack you may choose use one of the beasts attacks instead of your normal weapons attack.
Infused Animal Form. As a bonus action, your weapon morphs into its devil fruit beast form, retaining parts of the infused weapons appearance. The animal has its own intelligence and acts on its own turn directly after your own. All non-elemental damage the beast inflicts is based on the infused weapons damage type.
Additionally, the beast gains the weapon attack from the infused weapon as part of its own action list.
The beast listens to the person it perceives as it’s wielder.

sections.name: Gaseous Logia Infusion
sections.text:
Gaseous Logia fruits allow the weapon to harness intangible elemental properties.
Elemental Damage. The weapon deals an additional 1d6 elemental damage (closest to the fruits element as you can) on a hit and the weapons attacks ignores resistances to non-magical damage.
Extend Reach. The weapon’s range can increase by up to 10 ft. when you attack.
Fruit Spells. Using your weapon as the source of the spells, you may cast a spell from the devil fruits spell list using the Devil Fruit Infusion Charges table.

sections.name: Liquid Logia Infusion
sections.text:
Elemental Damage. The weapon deals an additional 1d6 elemental damage (closest to the fruits element as you can) on a hit and the weapons attacks ignores resistances to non-magical damage.
Fruit Effect. With your DM’s help, the weapon gains one feature from the fruit’s stat sheet. The feature cannot be the fruit’s awakening or any that would grant the user a resistance or immunity.
Fruit Spells. Using your weapon as the source of the spells, you may cast a spell from the devil fruits spell list using the Devil Fruit Infusion Charges table.

sections.name: Solid Logia Infusion
sections.text:
Elemental Damage. The weapon deals an additional 1d6 elemental damage (closest to the fruits element as you can) on a hit and the weapons attacks ignores resistances to non-magical damage.
Shattering Impact. On a hit, the weapon creates fragments or spikes of solid material around the target, dealing 1d6 damage to creatures within 5 feet.
Fruit Spells. Using your weapon as the source of the spells, you may cast a spell from the devil fruits spell list using the Devil Fruit Infusion Charges table.

sections.name: Devil Fruit Prototype
sections.text: With your dungeon master’s permission when you gain this feature, infuse a prototype devil fruit into your weapon. If you do so, roll on the devil fruit generation tables in Chapter 6: Devil Fruits.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two Ability Scores of your choice by 1. Alternatively, you can take a feat listed in Chapter 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Additionally, when you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can do one of the following, representing the increased power of your infused item:
Replace one cantrip you learned from this class’s Devil Fruit Infusion feature with another cantrip from the devilforged spell list.
Replace the feature on your weapon from the Infused Devil Fruit feature with one feature from another infusion.
If this change makes you ineligible for any of your Sea Devil’s Emanations, you must also replace them now, choosing emanations for which you qualify.

features.name: Fiendish Assimilation
features.text:
At 11th level, your devil fruit item develops immense newfound powers. Choose one 6th-level power (spell) from the devilforged spell list as this new power.
You can cast your Fiendish Assimilation power (spell) once without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest before you can do so again.
At higher levels, you gain more devilforged spells of your choice that can be cast in this way: one 7th-level spell at 13th level, one 8th-level spell at 15th level, and one 9th-level spell at 17th level. You regain all uses of your Fiendish Assimilation when you finish a long rest.
Alternatively, you can choose to incorporate or “steal” the essence of other great Devil Fruit powers into your infused item. When you see a Devil Fruit spell or spell effect within 30 feet of you, you may use your reaction to “store” a portion of the energy of that spell into your infused item, making it your new Fiendish Assimilation spell. The maximum level of the spell stolen must be equal to your current Fiendish Assimilation spell level. For example, if you are 13th level, you can only steal up to 7th-level spells created by a Devil Fruit power and store them into your infused item.
If you wish to remove the stolen Devil Fruit spell and return to using your original Fiendish Assimilation spell, you must spend 1 hour during a short or long rest removing the essence of the stolen spell and return the power of your original chosen Fiendish Assimilation spell. You cannot use the stolen spell again once it is removed from your infused item, unless you steal it again using this feature.

features.name: Devil’s Bounty
features.text: At 20th level, you can release a surge of energy from within your Devil Fruit-infused item, allowing you to regain expended power (spell) slots. To do so, you must spend 1 minute focusing on your infused item in order to regain all your expended spell slots from your Devil Fruit Infusion (Spellcasting) feature. Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

entries.name: Blade Smithing
entries.flavor: Devilforged who prioritize infusing their weapons for dueling and close-combat. This grants you enhanced damage, weapon proficiency, and fighting potential.

features.name: Devil’s Branding
features.text:
Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to burn a special brand or mark onto someone. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target is cursed by the devil’s brand for 1 minute. The curse ends and the brand disappears early if the target dies, you die, or you are incapacitated. Until the curse ends, you gain the following benefits:
You gain a bonus to damage rolls against the branded target. The bonus equals your proficiency bonus.
Any attack roll you make against the branded target is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
If the branded target dies, you regain hit points equal to your devilforged level + your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 hit point).
You can’t use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Hell’s Duelist
features.text:
At 1st level, you acquire the training necessary to effectively arm yourself for battle. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial melee weapons.
The experience you have gained in working with infusing various devil fruit powers into weapons has allowed you to become proficient with various weapons. When you finish a long rest, you can touch one weapon that you are proficient with and that lacks the two-handed property. When you attack with that weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls. This benefit lasts until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Echoing Strike
features.text:
At 6th level, you gain the ability to unleash a destructive wave of energy from your infused weapon. When you make a weapon attack on your turn against a creature, you may use a bonus action to extend its normal range by 10 ft. If the attack hits the target, any other creature of your choice within 5 feet of the target takes force damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Demonic Deflection
features.text: At 10th level, you are able to parry attacks made by your branded target in combat. If the target cursed by your Devil’s Branding hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to roll a d6. On a 4 or higher, the attack misses you, regardless of its roll.

features.name: Archdevil’s Branding
features.text: Starting at 14th level, you can spread your Devil’s Branding curse from a slain creature to another creature. When the creature cursed by your Devil’s Branding dies, you can apply the branding to a different creature you can see within 30 feet of you, provided you aren’t incapacitated, cursing it instead. When you apply the branding in this way, you don’t regain hit points from the death of the previously branded creature.

entries.name: Devil Bombardier
entries.flavor: As a Devil Bombardier, you specialize in infusing explosive devices with the powers of Paramecia and Logia devil fruits, creating devastating bombs that unleash chaos on the battlefield. Each bomb you create has a unique and unpredictable effect, combining raw elemental power with explosive force.

features.name: Tool Proficiency
features.text: When you choose this subclass at 1st level, you gain proficiency with Alchemist’s Supplies and Tinker’s Tools, essential for crafting and modifying your bombs.

features.name: Devilbomb Creation
features.text:
Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to create devilbombs. You can create one devilbomb per 10 minutes you spend undisturbed with your tinker tools. you can create a number of bombs equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses after a long rest.
Each time you create a devilbomb, roll on the “Explosive Infusions” table to determine the additional effect of the infusion. If a bomb you create calls for a creature to roll a saving throw use your spell save DC.
As an action, you can throw a devilbomb up to 30 feet. The bomb detonates on impact, dealing 2d6 thunder damage in a 10-foot radius. Creatures caught in the explosion must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking half damage on a successful save, and emits a thunderous boom audible out to 300 feet.

features.name: Enhanced Explosive
features.text: At 6th level, your devilbombs become deadlier and more refined. The maximum range for throwing your bomb increases to 60 feet, the damage of your devilbomb increases to 3d6, and the explosion radius extends to 15 feet.

features.name: Devastating Detonation
features.text: At 10th level, you further refine the destructive potential of your devilbomb. The damage increases to 4d6, and creatures that fail their saving throws are also stunned until the start of their next turn, as the concussive force disorients them.

features.name: Cataclysmic Blast
features.text:
At 14th level, you perfect the art of bomb-making, creating explosions that can devastate entire battlefields. Your devilbombs now deal 6d6 damage in a 20-foot radius and you can now throw two bombs as a single action, targeting separate areas within range. Each bomb still consumes one use, and each explosion is resolved separately.
Additionally, when rolling on the “Explosive Infusions” table, you may roll twice and choose which effect to apply, giving you greater control over the chaos of your creations.

features.name: Hellfire Artillery
features.text:
At 1st level, you gain proficiency in martial ranged weapons.
Additionally, you learn how to transform your infused item to fight for you. As a bonus action, you can use your infused item to create an artillery cannon that emerges from it. This cannon lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as a bonus action.
While your cannon is active, you can make a ranged spell attack against one creature within 60 feet of you as a bonus action. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 + your Charisma modifier in fire, cold, or lightning damage (your choice). When you reach the 10th level in this class, the damage increases to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier.
You can summon this cannon using this feature a number of times equal to your porficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Nether Scope
features.text:
At 6th level, your devil fruit item or weapon grants you enhanced sight and durability against flames. You gain the following benefits:
You gain darkvision up to 60 feet.
You gain proficiency in the Perception or Insight skill (your choice).
You gain resistance to fire damage.

features.name: Blinding Flare
features.text: At 6th level, the cannon you create with Hellfire Artillery can defend you and your allies. When you or a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is targeted by an attack, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage against that attack. After doing so, your cannon crumbles and disappears.

features.name: Exploding Shrapnel Shot
features.text:
Beginning at 10th level, your Hellfire Artillery cannon can produce burning sharpnel and embers when fired. While your Hellfire Artillery cannon is active, you may use this feature to cause one of the attacks you make with your cannon to explode by spending an action on the same turn as a part of firing the cannon. Whether the cannon hits the target or not, the shot detonates as a 5th-level fireball spell (using your spell save DC) centered on the target of your attack. Any creature that fails their save against this fireball also has their movement reduced by 10 feet until the end of their turns. Additionally, you may choose to make half of the damage any creature takes from this fireball piercing or slashing instead of fire.
Whenever you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Hellstorm Artillery
features.text:
When you reach 14th level, your Hellfire Artillery cannon grows even stronger. You gain the following benefits:
You can now create two cannons on your infused item with Hellfire Artillery as a bonus action, instead of just one, by expending an additional use of Hellfire Artillery. While you have two active cannons, when you spend a bonus action to attack with your cannon, both cannons can attack on your turn.
Your range with Hellfire Artillery increases to 120 feet.

entries.name: Gear Smithing
entries.flavor: Devilforged who prioritize infusing their equipment, armor, tools, or worn items are known as “Gear Smiths”. This grants you enhanced protection, proficiency, and physical ability.

features.name: Tool Proficiency
features.text: Starting at 1st level, you gain proficiency with Smith’s Tools. If you already have this tool proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of tool of your choice.

features.name: Armored Up
features.text:
At 1st level, you are able to use your infused equipment to grant you additional protection from harm. You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.
In addition, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while you have your infused devil fruit item equipped or held.

features.name: Abyssal Enhancement
features.text:
Starting at 6th level, you gain the ability to further enhance your physical abilities and defense using your infused equipment. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll’s effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Resilient Equipment
features.text: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feautre. Damage from magical weapons, haki-coated weapons, or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

features.name: Devilish Reconstruction
features.text:
When you reach 14th level, you are able to use your equipment to quickly and efficiently mend your injuries. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your devilforged level. Additionally, if you put a severed body part of yours back in place when you use this feature, the part reattaches.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Mechadevil
entries.flavor: As a Mechadevil, you have mastered the fusion of technology and devil fruit powers, constructing a powerful mech suit to aid you in battle. This suit enhance your abilities and turn you into a formidable force on the battlefield, capable of taking on foes far beyond your natural capabilities.

features.name: Mech Mending
features.text:
Gain the Mending cantrip when you choose this subclass.
In addition, you can channel your own vitality to repair your mech. As an action while within 5 feet of your mech, you can expend one or more of your Hit Dice. For each Hit Die expended, roll the die and multiply the result by your mech’s size factor, restoring that total as hit points to your mech. You regain no hit points yourself from Hit Dice spent in this way.

features.name: Mechadevil Mark 1
features.text:
Starting at 1st level, you construct a Mechadevil Suit: a suit of piloted armour you can control from within. While within 5 feet of your mech, you can use your action to enter it. If your mech isn’t within 5 feet of you but is on the same plane of existence, you can use your action to teleport it to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you and enter it as part of the same action.
Your Mechadevil Suit’s Strength score equal to your Charisma score and its Proficiency Score equals your Level. You can cast spells through your Mechadevil.
You can eject from your mech as a bonus action, landing in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of it. If your mech is reduced to 0 hit points, you eject, and the mech is destroyed. A destroyed mech can’t be piloted or teleported to you, and the mending spell has no effect on it.
When you are not piloting the mech and it has at least 1 hit point, you can mentally command it (no action required) to follow you. The mech moves on your initiative count (immediately after your turn) and uses its movement to approach within 10 ft. of you, avoiding hazards and obstacles to the best of its ability. If the mech cannot reach you due to an obstacle or terrain, it stops at the nearest safe space.

features.name: Mechadevil Mark 2
features.text:
At 6th level, your training for combat with your mech is rewarded. You gain proficiency with martial weapons.
Additionally, you may mount 2 specialised weapons onto your Mechadevil Suit. While piloting your mech, you can use a action to activate one of the weapons you chose. You may switch out any amount of weapons for new ones during a long rest.
Swarm Cannons. When you activate this weapon, both cannons fire a swarm of 16 missiles at a creature or object within 90 feet of you. Each dart hits a creature of your choice that you can see within range. A single missile deals 1d4 fire damage to its target. The darts all strike simultaneously, and you can direct them to hit one creature or several. Each creature targeted must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell save DC or take the damage of all missile directed at them.
Incinerator Beam. When you activate this weapon, the mech releases a blast of searing energy in a 15- foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw against your Spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d6 fire damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage.
Lightning Lance. When you activate this weapon, you unleash a lance of lightning in a line 30 ft. long and 5 ft. wide. Creatures in the line must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell save DC, or take 4d8 lightning damage.
Railcannon. When you activate this weapon, you fire a hypervelocity slug at a target you can see within 300 ft. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 5d10 piercing damage.
Cyclone Assault. When you activate this weapon, your Mechadevil begins a high-speed rotational assault. Each creature within 10 ft. of you must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d8 thunder damage. On a success, a creature takes half damage.
Power Fist. When you activate this weapon, you slam a fist charged with explosive power towards a creature or object within 5 feet of you. Make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes thunder damage equal to 5d8 + your mech’s Strength modifier and is pushed up to 10 feet away from you.
Additionally, your Mechadevil Suit can attack with a weapon attack above and a mech strike on the same turn.

features.name: Devil Reactor
features.text: At 10th level, you upgrade your Mechadevil’s reactor. The damage rolls of your Mechadevil’s Mech Strike attack increase by 2d8 and your Mechadevil gains a flying speed of 40 feet.

features.name: Overclock Devil Reactor
features.text:
At 14th level, you can overcharge your Mechadevil’s reactor as a last-ditch effort. When your Mecha is reduced to 0 hit points while you’re piloting it, you can cause it to self-destruct if you aren’t incapacitated (no action required). Alternatively, you can use your action while within 60 feet of your Mechadevil to doom it early, causing it to self-destruct.
When your Mechadevil self-destructs, you eject if you were piloting it, landing in an unoccupied space you can see within 60 ft. of it, and your mech explodes. Your mech is destroyed, and each creature within 30 ft. of it must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 12d8 fire damage and 2d8 force damage. On a success, a creature takes half damage.

entries.name: No Mi Trainer
entries.flavor: As a No Mi Trainer, you specialize in blending Zoan and Logia devil fruits to create powerful elemental beasts. Through the combination of beastly ferocity and raw elemental power, your creations become formidable allies on the battlefield, growing stronger and gaining new abilities with each advancement.

features.name: Tool Proficiency
features.text: When you choose this subclass at 1st level, you gain proficiency with Alchemist’s Supplies and Tinker’s Tools, essential for synthesizing compounds to control and enhance your beasts.

features.name: Bloodline Beast Synthesis
features.text:
Starting at 1st level, you can create 3 different bloodline beasts by combining Zoan and Logia devil fruit traits. You infuse a Zoan form with a chosen Logia element to create a monster that embodies both physical and elemental abilities.
You may only have one beast out at a time, otherwise their spirit and bodies are infused in tiny white stars. As an action, you may summon a beast from a star, reforming itself within 30 ft. of you. If a beast is already in play the active beast is recalled back into it’s star. You may recall all beasts using a Bonus Action.
In combat, the bloodline shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are incapacitated, the bloodline beast can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.
If your bloodline beast’s feature calls for a creature to roll a saving throw, use your spell save DC. Your created bloodline beast cannot be killed. However, until they are healed or recover naturally after 1d8 hours, their form transforms into a red star.
You may create 1 additional bloodline beast at 6th level, 12th level, and 18th level.

features.name: Enhanced Combat Efficiency
features.text:
At 6th level, your beast’s combat abilities are significantly enhanced, making it a more effective combatant. Choose one of the following enhancements for each of your beasts:
Melee Empowerment: Your beast’s melee attacks deal an additional die of damage.
Heightened Reflexes: Your beast gains a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws.
Unyielding Might: Your beast’s attacks now have a chance to hinder enemies. The target must succeed on a strength saving throw against your beasts strength or they are knocked prone or pushed them back 10 feet (your choice).
Resistance Shatter: Choose a damage type other than force you deal with your beast’s abilities. They now ignore resistances to that damage type when using their abilities, unless the resistance is granted by Haki.
Fast Action: Your beast now activates their beast’s element feature faster. Feature that cost an action now cost a bonus action.
Second Chance: When your beast drops to 0 hitpoints, instead of transforming into a red star as stated in the Bloodline Beast Synthesis feature, they instead drop to 1 hitpoint. This feature recharges on a short or long rest.

features.name: Tactical Evolution
features.text:
At 10th level, your beast undergoes Tactical Evolution, further boosting its combat capabilities. Choose one of the following upgrades for each of your beasts:
Relentless Assault: Your beast gains an extra attack on its turn.
Burst Attack: Your beast’s melee attacks now create an area-of-effect burst, hitting multiple enemies within 5 feet of the target for an amount of damage equal to it’s proficiency bonus.
Adaptive Defense: Your beast gains resistance to two types of damage other than force.
Steadfast Senses: With the help and approval of your DM, choose three of the following conditions: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Stunned. Your beast is now immune to that condition.

features.name: Supreme Combat Mastery
features.text:
At 14th level, your beast reaches the pinnacle of its combat effectiveness, gaining Supreme Combat Mastery. This feature allows your beast to operate at peak performance, pushing its abilities beyond normal limits. Choose one of the following mastery upgrades for each beast:
Frenzied Rampage: As a reaction, your beast can enter a frenzied state once per combat encounter, gaining advantage on all attack rolls and dealing critical hits on rolls of 19-20 for 1 minute. After the frenzy ends, the beast becoming stunned, regaining control of itself at the end of it’s next turn.
Elemental Overdrive: Grant the bloodline beast immunity to its own beast’s element’s resistance type or removes the vulnerability of its element.
Perfected Guardian: Your beast’s presence on the battlefield inspires allies, granting all allies within 30 feet a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws while the beast is active. Additionally, the beast gains an extra 20 hit points.
Unholy Infusion: Choose one additional beast’s element to infuse into your bloodline beast.

entries.name: Sea Devil’s Emanations
entries.text: These features grant you additional abilities as a Devilforged, assuming you meet their prerequisite. You may take a number of these emanations equal to the value shown on the Emanations Known column of the Devilfoged table, starting at level 2.

options.name: Agonizing Blast
options.text: When you cast eldritch blast, add your charisma modifier to the damage it deals on a hit.

options.name: Chilling Blast
options.text: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your eldritch blast, you can reduce that creature’s speed by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.

options.name: Demonic Protection
options.text: You can cast mage armor on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.name: Devil’s Sight
options.text: You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.

options.name: Fiendish Vigor
options.text: You can cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.name: Mask of Many Faces
options.text: You can cast disguise self at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.name: Misty Visions
options.text: You can cast silent image at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.name: Repelling Blast
options.text: When you hit a creature with eldritch blast, you can push the creature up to 10 feet away from you in a straight line.

options.name: Silver Tongue
options.text: You gain proficiency in the Deception and Persuasion skills.

options.name: Sniping Blast
options.text: When you cast eldritch blast, its range is 300 feet.

options.name: Stable Infusion
options.text: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell.

options.name: Thief of Five Fates
options.text: You can cast bane once using a devilforged spell slot. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Vacuum Blast
options.text: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your eldritch blast, you can move that creature in a straight line 10 feet closer to yourself.

options.name: Beast Speech
options.text: weapon You can cast speak with animals at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.name: Burning Blood
options.text: weapon As your logia-infused item begins to enhance the elements within your body, you gain nearly endless energy. You no longer need to sleep and can’t be forced to sleep by any means. To gain the benefits of a long rest, you can spend all 8 hours doing light activity, such as training with your item or keeping watch.

options.name: Enhanced Zoan Bond
options.text: weapon You can communicate telepathically with your summoned zoan creature and perceive through its senses as long as you are on the same plane of existence. Additionally, while perceiving through your summoned zoan creature’s senses, you can also speak through it in your own voice, even if your zoan infusion beast form is normally incapable of speech.

options.name: Greater Logia Powers
options.text: weapon You gain additional powers from your logia-infused item. Choose two 1st-level spells from the Hybrid, Chemist, or Tinkerer spell lists that deal cold, fire, lightning, acid, or thunder damage. These become Devilforged spells for you and don’t count against your number of known spells.

options.name: Greater Zoan Form
options.text:
weapon When you summon your zoan infusion beast form, you infuse the summoned zoan creature with greater power in its form, granting the creature the following benefits:
As a bonus action, you can command your summoned zoan creature to make an attack against an enemy within its range, using its reaction.
The summoned zoan creature’s weapon attacks are considered magical for the purpose of overcoming immunity and resistance to nonmagical attacks. When your summoned zoan creature takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant it resistance against that damage.

options.name: Improved Paramecia Weapon
options.text: weapon Your paramecia-infused weapon gains a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a magic weapon that already has a bonus to those rolls.

options.name: Zoan Regeneration
options.text: weapon Whenever you regain hit points while your summoned zoan creature is within 100 feet of you, treat any dice rolled to determine the hit points you regain as having rolled their maximum value for you.

options.name: Bestial Summon
options.text: weapon Your summoned zoan creature gains a +1 to its attack and damage rolls, and a +1 to its Armor Class.

options.name: Cloak of Shadows
options.text: When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become invisible until you move or take an action or a reaction.

options.name: Exhausting Presence
options.text: You can cast slow once using a devilforged spell slot. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Ice Tomb
options.text:
weapon As a reaction when you take damage, you can entomb yourself in ice, which melts away at the end of your next turn. You gain 10 temporary hit points per devilforged level, which take as much of the triggering damage as possible. Immediately after you take the damage, you gain vulnerability to fire damage, your speed is reduced to 0, and you are incapacitated. These effects, including any remaining temporary hit points, all end when the ice melts.
Once you use this emanation, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

options.name: Maddening Frequency
options.text:
As a bonus action, you can emit a sound frequency from your infused item which negatively influences the minds of other creatures around you. The sound can be heard by any creation 5 feet away from your in every direction, but not in total cover. It lasts until you’re incapacitated or you dismiss it as a bonus action.
The radius of sound gives you advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks but disadvantage on all other Charisma checks. Any other creature that starts its turn in the radius around you takes thunder damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 0 damage).
Once you use this emanation, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

options.name: Ricocheting Strike

options.name: Alluring Mist
options.text: You can cast compulsion once using a devilforged spell slot. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Relentless Mark
options.text: Your curse created by the hex spell or by a devilforged feature of yours creates a temporary bond between you and your target. To teleport in this way, you must be able to see the cursed target.

options.text: You can cast freedom of movement once on yourself without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

options.name: Visions of Chaos
options.text: You can cast confusion once using a devilforged spell slot. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

This effect may only occur once per creature, refreshing on that creature if they take a long rest.

options.name: Shadow Speech
options.text: You can cast speak with dead at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.name: Spring Step
options.text: You can cast jump at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.name: Zero-Gravity Step
options.text: You can cast levitate on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.name: Elemental Strike
options.text: weapon When you hit a creature with your infused logia weapon, the creature takes extra elemental damage of a type associated with your infused fruit, equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

options.name: Powerful Summon
options.text: weapon, Bestial Summon Your summoned zoan creature gains a +2 to its attack and damage rolls, and it gains an amount of temp HP each time you summon it equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

options.name: Ricocheting Maelstrome
options.text: Infused weapon, Ricocheting Strike The Extra Attack of your Ricocheting Strike emanation now grants two extra attacks rather than one.

options.name: Awakened Logia Powers
options.text: weapon, Blooming Logia Powers You gain additional powers from your logia-infused item. Choose two 4th-level spells and one 5th-level spell from the Hybrid, Chemist, or Tinkerer spell lists that deal cold, fire, lightning, acid, or thunder damage. These become Devilforged spells for you and don’t count against your number of known spells.

options.name: Beast Adaptation
options.text: weapon, Shared Zoan Transformation Your symbiosis with the beasts living in your armory grows even stronger, allowing you 1 more Hybrid Option and an additional use of your Hybrid Form per long rest.

options.name: Blast and Strike
options.text: Infused weapon When you use your action to cast a spell, you may make one attack with your infused weapon as a bonus action.

options.name: Logia Recharge
options.text: weapon For any emanations that grant the use of a spell once per long rest, you may cast them once per short rest instead.

options.name: Monstrous Submission
options.text:
weapon

options.name: Shroud of Shadow
options.text: You can cast invisibility at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.name: Superior Fiendish Assimilation
options.text: weapon You may have two 6th-level Fiendish Assimilation spells chosen or stored instead of just one. You may cast each of your 6th-level Fiendish Assimilation spells once per long rest.

options.name: Supreme-Grade Paramecia Weapon
options.text: Infused weapon, Ultimate Paramecia Weapon Your paramecia infused weapon gains a +5 bonus to its attack and damage rolls, unless it is a weapon that already has a higher bonus to those rolls. Additionally, you deal an additional 2d8 force damage with your paramecia infused weapon.

options.name: Sea Devil’s Duelist
options.text: You gain the Dueling fighting style.

options.name: Wrathful Weapon
options.text: You can cast one of the following spells using a devilforged slot: Searing Smite, Wrathful Smite, or Blinding Smite. Once you do so, you can’t do so this way again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Extended Strike
options.text: When using your echoing strike, your range extension bonus increases from 10 feet to 15 feet.

options.name: Sharpened Blade
options.text: You can choose to make your infused weapon’s damage die a d10 (the damage die for weapons with the versatile property becomes a d12 when wielded with two hands), regardless of its form.

options.name: A Thousand Slices
options.text: You can cast steel wind strike once using a devilforged spell slot, using your infused weapon as a component. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Blast Hopping
options.text: If you are hit by your own bomb’s blast zone, you may choose to be flung in a direction opposite of the bomb’s explosion radius. When you are flung, you travel 15 ft. away from your current spot, landing on your feet. You ignore opprotunity attacks when being flung.

options.name: Twin Explosion
options.text: When you throw a bomb, you may also throw an additional bomb. The second bomb can land anywhere of your choice within 15 ft. of the original.

options.name: Used to the Burn
options.text: Gain resistance to any self inflicted damage from features or spells you cast.

options.name: Bigger Boom
options.text: You can cast Flame Strike once for free. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Short Fuse
options.text: You may choose to detonate your bombs in your grip. If you do so, the damage of the bomb is doubled.

options.name: Blessed Bow
options.text: If your infused weapon is a longbow, you can create an arrow out of pure energy when attacking with it. Additionally, you make this enhanced attack at advantage if the target creature is a devil fruit user.

options.name: Quickened Shot
options.text: You can cast Magic Missile once for free. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest. Additionally, you may cast Magic Missile using a devilforged spell slot.

options.name: Blast Shot
options.text: You can cast Fireball once for free. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Force Cannon
options.text: If your infused weapon is a firearm or gun of some kind, you can choose to deal force damage for its damage type when you hit with it.

options.name: Lightning Cannon
options.text: If your infused weapon is a firearm or ranged weapon, you can cast lightning arrow using a devilforged spell slot. You can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

options.name: Greater Armor Infusion
options.text: You are able to infuse any suit of armor with your Devil Fruit Infusion to make it your Infused Item. When you do so, you are now proficient with that suit of armor. You remain proficient with it until the infusion is removed or you no longer have this emanation.

options.name: Jack of all Tools
options.text: You gain advantage on all checks using tools.

options.name: Countermeasures
options.text: You can cast Absorb Elements and Shield each once for free. You can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

options.name: Reinforced Armor
options.text: You can cast Armor of Agathys at your highest spell level once for free per long rest.

options.name: Digitigrade Joint Upgrade

options.name: Reactive Armor
options.text: You can cast Hellish Rebuke at your highest spell level once for free per long rest.

options.name: Intigrate Weapons

options.name: Reinforced Hull
options.text: Your mechadevil gains resistance to fire and cold damage, and heals from lightning damage while in combat.

options.name: Mecha Jets
options.text: You mechadevil’s flying speed increased by 20 feet.

options.name: Defensive Stance
options.text: When you summon a Bloodline Beast from a star, it gains 15 temporary hit points.

options.name: Bloodline Devil
options.text: You may infuse a Devil Fruit into your Bloodline Beast like it is a weapon using the Infuse Devil Fruit feature.

options.name: Power Surge
options.text: When you summon a Bloodline Beast from a star, it is effected by the haste spell until the start of your next turn.

options.name: Dueling Partner
